instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the 1 tbsp salt.
Meanwhile, slice the sausage on a slant into 1/4 inch pieces. Slice the onion and both peppers into thin strips, about 1/4 inch wide. Mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, stir together 1/2 cup ketchup, 3 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 1 tbsp soy sauce.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook for the time on the package, until it's al dente. Scoop out 1/2 cup of the pasta water into a mug, then drain the spaghetti.
While the spaghetti cooks, heat 2 tbsp oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's browned at the edges.
Add the onion and peppers and cook for 3 minutes, stirring often, until the onion is soft and see-through. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour the ketchup mixture over the vegetables and sausage. Let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring, until it darkens a little and smells less sharp.
Add the spaghetti and 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta water. Toss with tongs for 2 minutes, until the sauce coats every strand. If it looks dry, stir in a splash of the pasta water.
Season with the black pepper. Serve with hot sauce on the side for the adults.
method_notes: Doobydobap (4.0 from 282 ratings) is the lead: sausage browned first, then onion and peppers, ketchup mixed with a savory sauce and soy sauce, and the pasta tossed in. Japan Taste and RecipeTin Japan add a splash of pasta water and a little time for the ketchup to cook down, which is used here. Butter and Parmesan, which all three finish with, are left out to keep it dairy-free, and Worcestershire stands in for the bulldog sauce. Hot sauce is served at the table.
